newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia trade union membership falls.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia trade union membership falls.

text.p: The Australian Bureau of Statistics released figures on Monday showing that trade union membership in 1996 declined to 31 percent of Australia's 7.06 million workers aged 15 years and over.
The annual survey, generally compiled in August each year, found that 1996 union membership fell from 33 percent of the workforce in 1995 and 35 percent in 1994.
"The proportion of employees who were trade union members in connection with their main job has been steadily declining since August 1986," the bureau said.
"Between August 1986 and August 1996, the level of trade union membership reported by employees declined by around one-third (15 percentage points)," the bureau said.

In the 1996 survey, the electricity, gas and water supply industry recorded the highest rates of trade union membership with 70 percent of male employees and 38 percent of female employees belonging to a union.
The lowest rates of union membership were recorded in the agriculture, forest and fishing industry with seven percent of male employees and five percent of female employees belonging to a union.
